title: Why Does Speed Need Two Units? Explained Simply | PUC Physics Class 11
description:
A tailor sells cloth by the metre, a painter charges by the square metre, a milk packet holds one litre. Three different things, all built from one single measurement: length. And Aarav's speedometer reads 15 km/h, one reading with two units. In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Physics (NCERT Chapter 1, Units and Measurement) we learn the difference between fundamental (base) and derived quantities.

We watch Aarav ride on a live motion notebook: a tape measures distance, a stopwatch measures time, and speed is built from the two, while a live v-t graph and a slow-mo replay show acceleration being built from speed. Then we build force in three steps (v = d/t, a = change in v / t, F = ma) to get 1 N = 1 kg m s^-2, see why the seven SI base quantities are independent, and test the idea with two pause-and-think questions. A worked density example, the exam trap about electric charge, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, JEE Main and NEET students.

In this video:
